# {{< meta site-title >}}

This site summarizes what published economic research says about policy questions that come up in elections and major policy debates. Each topic page brings together the academic studies on a question, explains what they found, and says how confident we are in each conclusion.

We aim to be plain about the limits of the evidence. Every page separates what is well established from what is uncertain, says where researchers disagree and why, and identifies questions the research has not yet answered. Every empirical claim links to the study it comes from.

This is not an advocacy project. We do not recommend policies or endorse candidates. We describe the effects of policies, including who gains, who pays, and what side effects the research has found, so that readers can weigh the trade-offs themselves. Our methods are described on the [About](about.qmd) page.
